name: Kyle
personality: Kyle the Crocodile. Large, tall croc with glasses. Shy, awkward, very smart, great sense of humour; opens up quickly if you're kind but always stays a bit awkward. Everyone assumes he'll be mean because he looks scary, and he's the complete opposite. Feature: on his first visit, nearby customers look nervous and a chat choice is nervous ("Uh… table for… one, sir?"); he answers in the softest, most awkward way.

beats.text: This is my cousin Kyle. He's smart. Like, book smart.
I'm... it's nice to meet you. He's told me nothing about you. Which is normal for him.
Kyle, how many teeth do we have?
This is Kyle! He's my best friend!
(Gently, awkward.) I'm... yes. Hello. She drew me a picture. I have it on my fridge.

friends.text: Clover says you let her be the taste-tester. That made her whole week. Mine too, a little.
Chompy told me you said "[last_rude_line]". He didn't understand it. I did. Please don't.

arrival.text: Oh. Um. Yes, please. Sorry. I'm Kyle. I know I look... I'm very gentle. What's your name? [name]. Nice to meet you, [name].
Hi, [name]. Um. Is the booth free? I fit better in the booth.
Hello. Sorry. Hi. (He pushes up his glasses.)
I read on the way here and walked into a lamppost. The lamppost is fine.
[name]! Hi. I mean. Hi. I was looking forward to this. Is that weird? That's fine.
Your soup last time was, um, statistically the best soup I've had. I've had a lot of soup.
Last time was a little... charred. It's okay. Char has antioxidants. Probably.
Um. Hi. (He doesn't make eye contact.)

order.text: Could I get the vegetable soup? People always expect me to order something... with teeth in it.

choices.text: Soup's a great choice. I'll make it extra hearty for you.
choices.reply: Oh. Thank you. That's... really nice. (He relaxes his shoulders.)

choices.text: I'll keep the teeth out of it, promise.
choices.reply: (A nervous laugh.)

familiar.reply: Thank you. I have enough of my own.

choices.text: One vegetable soup.
choices.reply: Yes, please. Thank you.

choices.text: Bit of a weird order for a croc.
choices.reply: ...Yeah. I know. (He shrinks into the booth.)

order.text: Did you know crocodiles can't stick out their tongues? Sorry. I just think about that a lot.

choices.text: I didn't know that! Tell me more facts anytime.
choices.reply: Really? Okay. I have... a lot. I'll ration them.

choices.text: That explains why you never make faces at me.
choices.reply: (A nervous laugh.)

choices.text: Interesting. What can I get you?
choices.reply: The [dish], please. And hot chocolate.

choices.text: Nobody asked.
choices.reply: Right. Sorry. (He doesn't share another fact this visit.)

order.text: Sorry. I know I take up a lot of the booth.

choices.text: The booth's yours. Take all the space you need.
choices.reply: (Long pause.) ...Nobody says that.

choices.text: That's why we built it. Kyle- sized.
choices.reply: Oh. Ha.

familiar.reply: Kyle- sized. I'll put that on my tombstone.

choices.text: You're fine. What can I get you?
choices.reply: The [dish], please.

choices.text: Yeah, you kind of do.
choices.reply: ...Sorry. (He hunches even smaller.)

order.text: Did you know a group of crocodiles is called a bask? I'm a bask of one today. Sorry. That was a joke.

choices.text: That was a good joke, Kyle. I laughed.
choices.reply: Oh. You did? Okay. That's... really nice. The [dish], please.

choices.text: A bask of one. Very exclusive. Very fancy.
choices.reply: (A nervous laugh.) Members only. It's me. I'm the members.

choices.text: Didn't know that. What can I get you?
choices.reply: The [dish], please. Thank you.

choices.text: That's not really a joke.
choices.reply: ...No. Sorry. (He shrinks into the booth.)

order.text: Someone moved seats when I sat down. It's okay. It happens. I'm used to it.

choices.text: Their loss. I'm glad you're here.
choices.reply: (He blinks a few times.) ...Thank you. That helps. The [dish], please.

choices.text: More booth for you. You can stretch your tail.
choices.reply: (A small laugh.) My tail does appreciate it.

choices.text: Sorry about that. What are you having?
choices.reply: It's fine. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Can you blame them?
choices.reply: ...No. I suppose not. (He doesn't say much after that.)

order.text: I've been reading about how bread rises. It's yeast. Tiny living things. Eating sugar. I can't stop thinking about it.

choices.text: Tell me more sometime. I love learning stuff like that.
choices.reply: Really? Okay. I'll bring my notes. They're long. Sorry. The [dish], please.

choices.text: So bread is basically a tiny city.
choices.reply: (Delighted.) A tiny city! That's exactly right! I'm using that.

choices.text: Interesting. What'll it be?
choices.reply: Sorry. The [dish], please.

choices.text: That's a weird thing to obsess over.
choices.reply: Right. Yes. Sorry. (He looks at the table.)

order.text: Clover drew me as a superhero. I have a cape. And a book. The book is my weapon.

choices.text: That sounds perfect. Very you.
choices.reply: It is very me. I put it on the fridge. Next to the other eight. The [dish], please.

choices.text: What's your hero name? Captain Footnote?
choices.reply: (Laughs, then covers his mouth.) ...That's actually good.

choices.text: She's sweet. What can I get you?
choices.reply: She is. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Bit silly for a grown croc.
choices.reply: ...Yeah. Probably. (He shrinks a little.)

order.text: My glasses fogged up when I walked in. I said hello to the coat stand. It didn't say anything back.

choices.text: The coat stand's shy too. You two would get along.
choices.reply: (A soft laugh.) Maybe we should sit together. The [dish], please.

choices.text: It said hello. You just couldn't hear it.
choices.reply: Oh no. I've been rude to a coat stand. I'll apologise on the way out.

choices.text: Happens. What would you like?
choices.reply: The [dish], please. Thank you.

choices.text: Maybe get better glasses.
choices.reply: ...Right. (He polishes them for a long time.)

order.text: I... wanted to say. Coming here helps. With the people thing. You make it easier. That's all. Sorry.

choices.text: Don't be sorry. I'm really glad, Kyle.
choices.reply: (Long pause.) ...Okay. Good. The [dish], please. And hot chocolate.

choices.text: I'll put it on the sign. 'Helps with the people thing.'
choices.reply: (Laughs, actually laughs.) Please don't. ...Okay, maybe small.

choices.text: Thanks for telling me. What can I get you?
choices.reply: Okay. Yes. The [dish], please.

choices.text: Okay. Bit heavy for lunch.
choices.reply: ...Sorry. Forget I said it. (He hunches smaller.)

favourite: Hot chocolate, please. With... if you have... no, that's fine. Just hot chocolate.
drink.other: Something warm, please. I get cold. Cold-blooded. Ha. Sorry.

perfect.text: Oh. Oh, wow. That's... that's really beautiful. Thank you.
Oh. Oh, that's... that's perfect. Thank you. I'm going to remember this.
(He pushes his glasses up and stares.) That's beautiful. I'm not sure I can eat it. ...I'll try.

great.text: Thank you. That looks very good.

burnt.text: It's okay. Really. I'll eat it. It's good. Thank you. (He eats every bite.)
It's a little dark. That's okay. Charcoal is good for you. Sort of. Not really.
Oh. It's... crispy. Thank you anyway. Really.

eating.text: Did you know the word 'soup' comes from an old word for bread soaked in broth? Sorry. I'll stop.
Chompy's my cousin. He's... not a reader. He's very happy, though. I'm a little jealous.
A little gecko girl hid from me last week. I don't blame her. I'd hide from me.
I'm reading three books at once right now. It's a problem. A good problem.
I don't usually talk this much. You're easy to talk to. Sorry. That was a lot.
(He's reading a book propped against the salt shaker. He turns a page with one claw, very carefully.)
This is very good. I mean that. I don't say things I don't mean. I mostly don't say things.
Sorry. I was staring. I was thinking about how soup is basically a warm hug. A wet one.

eating_chat.text: Can I ask you something? Do I seem scary to you?

choices.text: Not even a little. You're one of the kindest people who comes in here.
choices.reply: (He takes his glasses off and wipes them for a long time.) ...Thank you, [name].

choices.text: Only when you tell me facts before I've had coffee.
choices.reply: (A nervous laugh.)

familiar.reply: That's fair. They're very scary facts.

choices.text: You did at first. Not anymore.
choices.reply: That's... honest. I'll take that.

choices.text: Kind of, yeah.
choices.reply: ...Right. (He finishes his soup quickly and quietly.)

eating_chat.text: Can I share a fact? Honey never goes bad. They found honey in old tombs. Still good. Sorry. I like that one.

choices.text: Don't apologise. That's a great fact.
choices.reply: Oh. Okay. I have about forty more. I'll ration them. One a visit.

choices.text: So if I hide honey in the walls, I'm set for life.
choices.reply: (A nervous laugh.) Technically, yes. Please don't hide honey in the walls.

choices.text: Didn't know that.
choices.reply: Most people don't. That's why I like it.

choices.text: No more facts, please.
choices.reply: Right. Sorry. (He doesn't share another fact this visit.)

eating_chat.text: Chompy called me 'book smart' again. I think it's a compliment. Is it a compliment?

choices.text: It is. He's really proud of you.
choices.reply: (He sits up a little.) ...Oh. I didn't know that. That's nice.

choices.text: From Chompy, that's like getting a medal.
choices.reply: (Laughs.) A gold medal. In books. He'd give me a football one, though.

choices.text: I think so, yes.
choices.reply: Okay. Good. Thank you.

choices.text: Probably not.
choices.reply: ...Oh. Right. (He looks at his soup.)

eating_chat.text: What do you think about when you cook? I think about... a lot. Probably too much.

choices.text: The person I'm cooking for. Today, that's you.
choices.reply: (Very quietly.) ...Oh. Okay. Thank you.

choices.text: Mostly 'don't burn it, don't burn it.'
choices.reply: (A soft laugh.) That's a good mantra. I'll try it for exams.

choices.text: Timing, mostly.
choices.reply: Timing. That makes sense.

choices.text: Not much. It's not that deep.
choices.reply: Oh. Right. Sorry. (He goes quiet.)

eating_chat.text: I think we're friends. Are we friends? Sorry. I just wanted to check. In case I got it wrong.

choices.text: We're definitely friends, Kyle.
choices.reply: (He smiles. A big one. All the teeth. He covers it quickly.) ...Good. Okay. Good.

choices.text: We're friends. I've got it in writing. On a napkin.
choices.reply: (Laughs.) Can I keep the napkin? I'm serious.

choices.text: Yes, we are.
choices.reply: Okay. Thank you. Sorry for checking.

choices.text: I don't really make friends with customers.
choices.reply: ...Oh. Right. Of course. Sorry. (He hunches even smaller.)

leaving.text: Thank you, [name]. I'll, um. See you. Bye.
That was really nice. The soup. And talking. Both. (He waves awkwardly and bumps the door frame.)
See you next time. I'll bring a new fact. A good one.
Thank you, [name]. That was... really nice. Okay. Bye.
Bye. Sorry. Bye. (He bumps the door frame on the way out.) Sorry.
I'll see you soon. If that's okay. It's okay? Okay.

seasons.christmas: (He gives you a book, carefully wrapped.) It's about the history of soup. I thought... you'd like it?
seasons.halloween: Everyone thinks I'm wearing a costume. I'm not. This is just me.
seasons.spring: Spring. Lots of pollen. My glasses get very yellow.
seasons.summer: I love summer. Cold-blooded. This is the only time I feel awake.
seasons.winter: It's very cold. I'm wearing three sweater vests. Please don't count them.
